utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Could we have the accused brought in, please? (Accused enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First, let's see whether the interpreters are prepared and make sure that everybody hears the Presiding Judge and the other judges when we speak. Does the Prosecution hear? Does the Defence hear? Mr. Blaskic, do you hear? GENERAL BLASKIC: Good morning, your Honour. I hear you fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. We can now resume the hearing and again have the witness brought in, Professor Pajic. Mr. Cayley, would you have the Professor brought in?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Merci. (Witness enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good morning, Professor. Would you please be seated. Did you have a good rest? Again the Tribunal thanks you for remaining available for this morning's hearing. We can -- I believe it was Mr. Nobilo who can now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Nobilo, I give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone. Professor Pajic (continued) Cross-examination by Mr. Nobilo

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, your Honours, esteemed colleagues, I wish to continue where we stopped yesterday. Dr. Pajic, if you remember, yesterday we were on document 10, Exhibit 38. This was the decree on border crossing and traffic in the border area of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in times of war or the immediate threat of war. So with your concurrence, could you give me your basic opinion on the status of who is a foreigner and who is not a foreigner according to this law, so we can proceed from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I shall try to continue where we broke off our discussion on this question yesterday. Very briefly, I wish to underline that my conclusion was based on provisions that imply a certain situation. To be quite clear, there is no explicit mention that the citizens of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina are foreigners in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, but there is a certain contradiction in certain provisions, and I got the impression that implicitly the citizens of The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina who do not reside in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna are treated as foreigners. We discussed it yesterday. Article 12 is relevant, and it says: "A citizen of the RBH carrying weapons or ammunitions into or out of the HZ H-B shall report the weapons and ammunition to the border police or military police at the state border". You have rightfully said that carrying arms into and out of the area was subject to permits, wasn't it, but what led me to claim that implicitly citizens of The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina are treated as foreigners is paragraph 2 of Article 12, where it says that: "Authorisation from the relevant administrative body of the HVO HZ H-B shall be required when carrying weapons and ammunition across the border". So the question that is raised here in my mind is why does a citizen of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina from paragraph 1, why is it not enough for him to have a permit, which he would possibly obtain from the competent authority in Sarajevo, namely the competent authority of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree that this is a good question, but isn't this a question of competence of certain organs, certain state organs, not a question of citizenship? Isn't that now a question of jurisdiction between a local organ and a federal organ related to permits, for example, for carrying weapons, not a question of citizenship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see from this that you actually agree with me that we are talking about what is implicitly said by certain provisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm asking you what you just said, one cannot draw a conclusion on citizenship on that basis. It is perhaps an illogical or wrong distribution of jurisdiction between the two. Do you understand the distinction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand the distinction, and it is true that it is a separation of jurisdiction, but also it is a fact that the HVO HZ H-B never had this kind of jurisdiction on the basis of the constitution of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: True, but you keep evading the issue of citizenship. Perhaps I can rephrase it. The citizens of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina who have permanent residence in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, do they also need a permit from the authorities of Herceg-Bosna? Do they have a different status from the citizens of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina who reside outside the area of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This distinction cannot be seen from this specific provision between persons residing on the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the other citizens of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we conclude that they have the same status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We can conclude that they have the same status, but I remind you once again that it is illogical that a citizen of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina who, let us assume, is travelling from Sarajevo through the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna asks the HVO HZ H-B for a permit to carry weapons, not the competent authority of his republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, yesterday I made eight separate objections based upon the fact that learned counsel kept interrupting the witness, and indeed now even Mr. Hayman is warning his colleague about this. I would request respectfully that Mr. Nobilo be reminded again that the witness be allowed to answer the questions that he is putting to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I would like the day to begin the way it ended yesterday, that the cross-examination be done properly, but the Presiding Judge also wants to move things forward. I would have to say that I saw your colleague moving his arm, Mr. Nobilo. You asked your question, you got an answer. I think that either this is a discussion between two deaf people and you draw the conclusions you want. Perhaps you want to move to another question. Then go to another question, if you do not mind. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I agree, but I think that we were close to reaching agreement. I wish to clarify matters. I do not want them to remain in the air. If it is clear to you, then everything is clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The trial is not an arbitration hearing, Mr. Nobilo. You ask your questions, you get answers, you draw the conclusions from that you like, and then you move to the next question. These discussions will go on for a long time. The issue will be brought up several times. Please, I said that we had to finish at 12.30, I will repeat this throughout this trial. With the deepest respect for cross-examination available to each of the parties. Mr. Nobilo, please start again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So we have come to the question of the distinction, distinction between the status of those who live been the territory of Herceg-Bosna and those who do not live under the territory of Herceg-Bosna. Can you give me a brief answer to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very briefly, the decree we are speaking about is not the decree on citizenship. It pertains to a specific procedure of crossing the State border and concretely this is an Article on carrying weapons, so in this procedure, in this treatment, I believe that by implication a citizen of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina is treated as a foreigner or as a quasi-foreigner. That expression is not used here, but he has to seek a permit from an organ which is not an organ of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a person residing in Herceg-Bosna, does that person have to seek that kind of permit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I imagine so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We move further on to document 11?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think you have already asked this question. Let us move to a different question. You have already asked that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The question having to do with the citizenship of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The entire transcript was transcribed. You have received the answer. I think we have to move forward. For fifteen minutes now we have been dealing with the same question. So I'm asking you to move forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. I have just said that we were moving on to document 11. That is a different decree. We have moved on to the next decree or law, so we have completed the previous one. So now it is document 11, the decree on implementing the law on the movement and residence of aliens. You have already spoken about that and I wish to draw your attention to Article 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have been following you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the light of the discussion we have had so far do you still think that this definition of an alien deviates from a consistency that you noted or is it in line with the previous decree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry. I am looking at the transcript and I have been trying to find what I said about this provision yesterday but I will try to repeat it. This provision, as I said, is in a way the product of indecisiveness in terms of passing a more decisive and definite norm on this matter. I said yesterday that an alien as provided for under this decree shall be any person who is not a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina and, argumentum ad contraria, as I said, it can be said that a citizen of The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina is at the same time "a citizen of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna". Is that the question that you are aiming at?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Document 12 of Exhibit 38. This is the decree on the implementation of the law on registering the domicile and residence of citizens in the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna. I just wish to draw your attention to Article 5. Please have a look at it. Could you give me your comment? In your opinion is this Article actually an obstacle in the path of ethnic cleansing or the results of ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a very sensitive area of the case. To try to link of concept of ethnic cleansing to these documents and the testimony of this witness is completely improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Could you reformulate your question, please? Please reformulate the question. We are now discussing the decree on document 12. I've just looked at it in the English version. You cannot ask information from the witness which he was not called to speak about by the Prosecutor. He is not here to judge as to whether or not this is part of the process of ethnic cleansing. Therefore, I ask you to reformulate your question so that you can get the answer you like, but please reformulate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You didn't understand me correctly. I didn't say that it was part of ethnic cleansing, but does this rule prohibit the results of ethnic cleansing from remaining permanent and lasting. So I said that this regulation was a way of annulling the results of ethnic cleansing. Look at Article 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry. I know you wish matters to move forward, but I really do not believe that this witness can comment on ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Absolutely: I grant the objection of the Prosecutor and ask you to move to another question if you can't ask this one in a different fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: All right. Then we'll move on. I wish to draw your attention to document 15 of Exhibit 38. Do you know whether we are talking about the decree on the rights and obligations of citizens temporarily working abroad concerning service in the armed forces in times of immediate threat of war or wartime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what page this is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 316, number 12. It is document number 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have found it. Okay. So it is the decree on the rights and obligations of citizens temporarily working abroad, etc. Do you know on the basis of your general knowledge or professional knowledge that Bosnia-Herzegovina had a similar law? How was it regulated on the rest of its territory? Are you aware of that? If not, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My comment to this -- my comment on this decree was that it mirrors the state-like behaviour of Herceg-Bosna, and that is why I cited it in my analysis. I can answer your question by saying yes. As far as I know, after I came to Great Britain at the end of the summer of 1992, I heard from the then information centre of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in London that some kind of directive was sent from Sarajevo to invite the citizens of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to give a material contribution for the Defence of the country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please let us now move on to document number 17. So this is the basic decision on establishing and proclaiming the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. Issue number 1, page 6. In fact, I wish to draw your attention to page 5 of number 1 and the preamble. With your permission I shall briefly read out the third paragraph of the preamble and I would like to hear your comment. In view of the nature of the state, unitary, federal, confederal, does this refer to the break-up of Bosnia-Herzegovina or establishing Bosnia-Herzegovina as a composite state, federal or confederal: "Having found that the existing political and state system does not ensure the Croat people their rights in Bosnia-Herzegovina and their rights to Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Croatian people are determined ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Ask your question, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This preamble, does it advocate the division of Bosnia-Herzegovina or establishing Bosnia-Herzegovina as a complex, a composite state in any form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the part of the preamble that you are referring to it is said explicitly that the Croatian people are establishing their state community on part of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is one conclusion, and I do not see that there's any scope for interpretation there. The State community is clearly defined, so according to general international law a State has a certain territory, a certain population and effective authority, and there is no point in quoting authorities on the basis of whose writings these provisions of international law and customary law and international practice are based. The second part of this section says that this kind of state community would transfer part of its rights to a federation of republics and would participate in certain joint institutions and services of mutual interest in the republic. If you ask me as a Professor of international law, this means opening the door to a confederacy with the other parts of this future Bosnia-Herzegovina and a confederacy by definition is not a state but an association of sovereign states.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My final question. So what would be your opinion as a Professor of international law having analysed all the legal documents of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna? As an international Professor what was your assessment, was this community a state or not? Briefly yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe that the witness has already answered this question yesterday in his final concluding remarks that run for some four pages in the transcript. It is simply a repeat of a question I have already asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, you did ask the question, but you asked it from your point of view. It is normal that the Defence would ask the question as well. It was a short question. There will now be an answer in light of what he said yesterday, but I cannot accept that objection. Mr. Nobilo, you can go on and I instruct the Professor to answer the question "yes" or "no", or if not that, at least briefly, because even the Defence asked you to answer very briefly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, later the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, had the characteristics of a state community, and in that process, which lasted some two or three years, there was a clear tendency of strengthening all the elements of a state community. What the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna lacked from the point of view of international law was international recognition, so they would fully qualify as a state. From that point of view we can say according to international law it was not a state. At the same time I have to warn you that this process of establishing, consolidating the statehood of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was interrupted by the Washington Agreement in March and April 1994, when at the insistence of the international community and, above all, the United States of America, a cease-fire was agreed upon, peace -- I must say this colloquially -- the Bosnian Croats and the Bosnian Muslims, and a federation of the Muslim and Croatian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina was established. That is the whole story.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pajic. Now my colleague, Mr. Hayman, will continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nobilo. Cross-examination by Mr. Hayman

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nobilo. Mr. Hayman, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Good morning, Dr. Pajic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First, I would like to ask some general questions concerning your preparation for your testimony here at the Tribunal. How many meetings did you have with representatives of the Prosecutor's Office in anticipation of your testimony and indeed preparing your study of the Narodni list documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first meeting with the office of the Prosecutor took place in February this year in The Hague, when I was informed of the problem and when I was asked to accept the role of an expert witness in these proceedings, that is to present my expert opinion regarding the legal documents of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna or rather the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. At the time I took with me -- let me note that this meeting in February in The Hague took one day, maybe one and a half, and then I took with me the documents that you have had occasion to see bound into four volumes of documents of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and I was given a clear indication of what it is that the Office of the Prosecutor expects of me and I undertook this obligation and started my studies. I worked on it in March and April, taking notes, analysing the documents, linking this with my own personal experiences and my personal knowledge about this area, and I have those notes somewhere, but I do not suppose you need such a detailed answer. Towards the end of April a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor visited me in London and then we had a two-day briefing when we went through my analysis which I had prepared by then. Then we met again in London for a day's meeting. As far as I can recall, this was three weeks ago. Finally, I came to The Hague last week expecting to be called to testify last week already. However, this was postponed for Monday 30th June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you have had some further meetings with representatives of the Prosecutor's office since you arrived here in The Hague last week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the course of last week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would those total half a day or a day in length?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was half a day, because the prosecutors were busy in the courtroom in connection with the testimony of my predecessor, the previous expert witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if my maths is correct, Professor, you have spent about five days in total discussing your testimony and the needs of the Prosecutor's office with them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you testified that either most or all of the documents you reviewed were contained in Exhibit 36, the four Narodni list volumes; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But not all; some were not taken from those volumes; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were documents, mostly official gazettes of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which I had in my possession, and I referred to them in my testimony, such as the constitution of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the decision of the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which, of course, is included in these volumes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the only documents that you were given by the Prosecutor's Office contained in Exhibit 36?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Will you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the only documents you have been given by the Office of the Prosecutor in connection with your study or review contained in Exhibit 36, the Narodni list volumes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but during our first meeting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 36 or 38? What document are you talking about here?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: 36, your Honour, four fat volumes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but during our first meeting I had occasion to see the text of the indictment against Mr. Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Exhibit 38, tab 1? How did you come by that document? Do you need that placed before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could that exhibit, your Honour, be placed before the witness? (Handed)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can see, these are the same documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: One moment, please. (Pause.) Which tab are you talking about here?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Tab 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Could you show that to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I just speak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It is to clarify matters. I mean, I can understand where my learned friend is trying to take this, but in essence this is the first document in the bundle that's before you in the file. It was provided to Dr. Pajic. It's not part of the Narodni list. It is the original unamended version of a document that later appears in an amended version in the Narodni lists. That is the documents, the very first document in the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I appreciate my colleague's assistance but I would actually like to question the witness about where he got the documents he studied. May I?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are referring to the document on establishing the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 38, tab 1. Do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that document published in the Narodni list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was not published in the Narodni list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were also given this document by the Prosecutor's Office. We have heard Mr. Cayley describe that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was given to me by the Office of the Prosecutor and in this exact form inserted into the cover of the first volume of these four volumes that you have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides that document and a copy of the indictment which you were either given or shown, were you provided with any other documents by the Prosecutor's office in connection with the study you undertook?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did your review of the four volumes which comprise collectively Exhibit 36 take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the number of hours or the number of days that I spent?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The question, Mr. Hayman, is this an important question for the Defence strategy? Is it very important, because for five or six minutes we are now talking about this document. If you think it's important, go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It goes to the process of his study, whether this is a scientific process, some other process, the origins of the information he reviewed, who selected them and so forth. I'm moving forward as quickly as I can, your Honour. There have been some questions and discussions with my learned counsel across the way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: But I'm moving forward as quickly as I can. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Not translated).

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Translation please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic says he is not hearing. Can you hear me, General Blaskic? GENERAL BLASKIC: Your Honour, your Honour, I cannot hear at all the questions put by my counsel. I can only hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That is not enough. You have got to be able to hear. First of all, Mr. Hayman, do you have a comment you would like to make about the technical issues here?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: For a period I was not receiving an English translation of your Honour. There was a gap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is important. I want this technical problem to be solved. Mr. Blaskic. GENERAL BLASKIC: I can hear well now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, do you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I suppose, Mr. Hayman, you would not like the Presiding Judge repeat his earlier intervention. I think you understood what he meant. We can go on now. If you feel that your client has not heard everything that you are saying, then you just start over again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I do not think that's necessary, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Dr. Pajic, in days or hours how long did you spend reviewing Exhibit 36?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't keep a very close track of the time, but I must say that these documents were before me all the time, to such an extent that even last week before coming to The Hague I think that I could by heart from memory give you the name of each of the documents in their order, when they were passed, and I could even quote much of those documents, but I really did not keep a close account of the time spent. After all, I'm not an employee of this Tribunal, nor am I engaged full-time, but throughout March, April and May I kept taking notes. I entered them into my computer. I went back to them. I revised my conclusions. I amended them and on. So it was an on-going process. Maybe that is the best way to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you spend several weeks engaged in this endeavour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't work on it every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, first of all allow the question to be asked and the witness has to answer after which you can intervene. Mr. Pajic, I myself asked that question. I think Mr. Hayman understood. Now I would like Mr. Pajic to answer, but as quickly as possible, that is answer Mr. Hayman's question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I spent analysing these documents certainly many weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Did you review any other material, such as secondary sources, articles, books and the like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everything that was relevant and linked to the current events in the region of Bosnia and Herzegovina, or rather the region that has been designated as Herceg-Bosna, I have been following events there and I am still following developments there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you conduct any field interviews in connection with your study?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit Bosnia and Herzegovina in connection with your study?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I visited Sarajevo in May and again in June I spent three days there. In May I was there as a consultant of an international non-government organisation, International IDA from Stockholm. Now in Sarajevo from 17th-21st June I was on a private visit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you made no effort to interview persons directly involved in the events and decrees and so forth in Exhibits 36 and 38; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Indeed I believed it was an assignment I was given to analyse the documents. I didn't feel it was necessary for me to engage in any kind of conversations with peoples living in the region there. In fact, I sought to ensure a certain degree of discretion in dealing with this matter, because I am following the work of the Tribunal, and I see that there is a kind of routing here and there and some lay interpretations that have nothing in common with what is actually happening in this court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have mentioned the decrees and decisions then necessary in Exhibit 38. Do you know who drafted them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean am I familiar with the persons who worked on these drafts? No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were copied in large part from other documents, perhaps from other countries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no reason -- I do not know what you mean under other countries, but I assume that the experiences that existed in the territory of the former Yugoslavia and its legislation were used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your review of our materials at your disposal, as you have described, did you determine to what extent the decrees and decisions in Exhibit 38 were actually implemented on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, I didn't have occasion to do that and, secondly, that was not my task to investigate to what extent these normative documents were implemented in practice. All I could see was that within the scope of normative activities one could conclude that the system of decision-making had such an effect that, as Mr. Nobilo and myself discussed yesterday, in some cases bodies or departments of the Croatian Defence Council functioned as kind of independent "ministries" or "administrative departments", but in quotation marks, but I do not have any personal knowledge from the field to what extent this was implemented in practice. All I can speak about are my impressions on the basis of reports in the media, but that is certainly not relevant in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you prepare a written report of your study or review?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I have in writing are my own notes, which I used while reading these documents, but I did not prepare any written report, and in the first conversation with the prosecutors this year in The Hague I asked and it was agreed that no written report was expected of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use your notes in connection with your presentations and briefings of the representatives of the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I did. I used my notes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then based on the feedback they gave you, did you take additional notes to assist you in your presentation to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The feedback, I must say, was back and forward, because the Prosecutor and I co-operated in this matter. Though suggestions came from the Prosecutor regarding further clarifications of this or that point, I frequently felt the need to brief the Prosecutor too regarding many questions that in view of my expert knowledge and my origins from Bosnia-Herzegovina I could familiarise them with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you prepare any charts or graphical aids to assist you in your work, in your briefings, or in your briefings of the Prosecutor's office representatives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you paid for your work or did you perform it gratis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For this work I received the fee of a consultant as prescribed by the rules applicable in the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it you were paid a fee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Consultancy fee, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now during your testimony have you also utilised some notes hand-written on some of the decisions and decrees in Exhibit 38?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for my own needs, of course, attached to each of these documents I made notes, a memo, I underlined some things, which is normal, I think, when you are analysing a text, put notes in the margins and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some of those notes prepared during your meetings and conferences with the Prosecutor's Office, based on the content of your discussions with those representatives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. If I thought something was important so when I went back home I could refer to it and study something in further depth, so I put down a note as a memo to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it when you undertook your review of Exhibit 36 and 38 you were aware of the charges against the accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In very general terms I must tell you. You see, I thought about this a great deal, and maybe this is the opportunity for me to say this. When one accepts such a delicate assignment there are necessarily certain morale dilemmas, no professional dilemmas, because we do what we know best, because, after all, at my age one can only do something one knows how to do. It's rather difficult to start learning. As for morale dilemmas, you see, I gave priority with respect to this project on the analysis of the documents of the normative situation regarding the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and throughout my study of this, though I did read the indictment very superficially, I knew very well that I had no personal relationship towards the accused, that I have absolutely no personal knowledge about the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I do not even carry in my mind the smallest dose of bitterness towards the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. I simply experience this whole situation that happened and that is still on-going in my homeland or the country that I come from. I have developed a certain attitude towards those developments, an attitude of professional curiosity. So please, I would like you to understand my engagement in this case in that sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think things will move a little quicker if you focus on my question and try to answer my questions as briefly as possible. The Prosecutor will have an opportunity to ask further follow-up questions. So my question was: were you aware of the charges against the accused when you undertook your review?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I realise we wish to move things forward. The indictment is a public document. It is accessible to the world. It is not the witness' special knowledge being aware -- this is not relevant, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: He may or may not have seen it just because it's a public document, your Honour, and it is very relevant for the line of questioning I'm going into. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would emphasise again this is a publicly available document. The sight of it is in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would suggest -- I think we are wasting time here. This is a public document. I think that you made an observation to the witness, Mr. Hayman. I could make one to you. You have been asking these questions for a long time now, of course, the context in which this testimony was gathered by the witness, and that is your right, but going back more specifically to the indictment, it is true that it has been published now for over a year, and since the time that Mr. Blaskic has been in The Hague. I would like us to go forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: From your review of the documents in Exhibits 36 and 38 were you able to draw any conclusions concerning the ability of an HVO field commander, military field commander, such as the commander of an operative zone, to appoint an HVO brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I didn't go that far in my analysis. I have already stressed that I am not an expert for military affairs, nor for military hierarchy, so that I couldn't make any conclusions in that respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does one of the decrees and decisions in Exhibit 38 state that the President or Presidency has that authority? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. To a point, commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So an operative zone commander would not have authority under these documents to appoint a brigade commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to look at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Could you tell us what document this is, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Will you refer to the document, Mr. Hayman, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I could assist my learned friend, it is, in fact, document 2, page 19, Article 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you: do you have that before you, Dr. Pajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What is the title of the document, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Decree on the armed forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. I have the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 2, page 19, Article 34?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shall I restate my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So under this Article would you agree that the President, not an operative zone commander, has the power and authority to appoint and dismiss brigade commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That falls under the jurisdiction of the President of the HZ H-B, the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without taking the time to refer to it, do you recall the decree on the district military prosecutors' offices?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall that the power to appoint those district military prosecutors was also vested in the President or the Presidency, not zone HVO military commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the decree on discipline, on disciplinary measures, regarding soldiers in the HVO, or shall we turn to it? That's tab 2, page 60.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I could correct my learned friend, the Rules of Military Discipline appear on page 37, so the witness is not confused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 60 is something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: How would you describe the document that begins on page 60?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The title of the document is "Mandatory Directive".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On, among other things, the possible pronouncement of penal sanctions for acts committed against the armed forces of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now this directive delineates some 35 or 40 offences; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I direct your attention to Article 38?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Article 38 of what document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. 238. It is on page 61 of tab 2. I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The last one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the last one. Why don't you take a moment to read it, please, to yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that this Article stipulates that disciplinary punishment applies or can apply only to listed offences that are punishable by less than three years, whereas listed offences punishable by more than three years are a matter of penal sanctions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can you make your question more simple, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll do my best. Under Article 238 a distinction is drawn between -- and I do not know how these phrases are being translated so I will identify the terms -- a distinction is drawn between penal sanctions and disciplinary punishment. Do you see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you tell us what document this is again, please? We're a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Of course, your Honour. Tab 2 of Exhibit 38, page 61, the last article on that page is Article 238. Dr. Pajic, do you see these two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you ask your question again. Since you mentioned three different texts, could you now make your question more concise?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes. Do you see Dr. Pajic, in Article 238 that it draws a distinction between "disciplinary punishment" and "penal sanctions"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is the distinction drawn that disciplinary punishment may only be imposed if the offence is punishable by less than three years of imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now are you familiar with the meaning of the term "disciplinary punishment" versus the term "penal sanctions" as used in Article 238?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it means, does it not, that penal sanctions can only be imposed by a court, such as a military court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In this case a military court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you also agree then that a zone commander, an HVO military commander of an operative zone, could not impose on any soldiers under his command any penal sanctions as that term is used and limited in Exhibit 238?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could intervene, I really do not believe that this witness can answer the question that is being posed from that provision. That is not why he was called here to give evidence. These are specific questions on military justice, of which the witness has already stated he has no special knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What I would say, your Honour, is he -- may I read one sentence of his direct testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please allow the Presiding Judge to speak to the objection. I do not agree with this objection of the Prosecutor. You cited all these documents, Mr. Cayley. Your witness analysed them. When your witness considered that he had real competence over an area he stated that. When he said that he had less competence in a certain area specifically in the military area he also stated it, and I criticised the Defence several days ago when it wanted to use the witness' answers when he said that he was not a military expert. I must have told the Defence that even if he was not a military expert, he could continue to testify. He is a Professor of law. Perhaps he is not a criminal -- an expert in criminal law like you, Mr. Cayley, but you cited the three documents. The Defence has the right at least to ask for an interpretation of that -- of those documents, and therefore I overrule your objection. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If you would work with me for a moment to identify at least for example purposes a few of the offences that are punishable by less than three year's imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you direct your attention to Article 204 on page 60?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The offence of disobeying a guard, do you see that is punishable by up to three year's imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up to three years, right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next page, the offence under Article 218 of avoiding registration, do you see that is punishable by only up to one year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or punishable by money, by paying a certain amount of money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you gave four general conclusions. The second general conclusion was the omnipresent role of the HVO in all state affairs. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now since you made that statement, you and Mr. Nobilo have had a discussion concerning the existence within the entity generally described as the HVO of both civil organs as well as a military organ or an army; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now when you made the statement that the HVO was omnipresent in all state affairs, were you including both civil and military elements or organs of the HVO when you used the term "HVO" in that context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that I tried to be quite precise when I was speaking about the omnipresent role of the HVO. I meant the decisive influence in the legislative area through the Presidency, then influence in terms of the executive and administrative government, a decisive role in the judiciary, in terms of the right to appoint courts, judges, to appoint and recall judges, and decisive influence in the defence of the country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And excluding the last item for the moment, the Defence of the country, all the other responsibilities and powers you just stated fell to civil organs or elements within the so-called HVO; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But not to waste time on looking for documents, but the HVO was in charge of appointing military courts. Is that not right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the break we can find that decree and save time and look at it after the break. For the moment let me ask you: at any time reflected in any of the documents in Exhibit 38 did all authority within the HZ H-B pass to the military body within the HVO, that is the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time reflected by any of the documents in Exhibit 38, in other words as of the date of any of the documents in Exhibit 38, did all authority within the HZ H-B pass to the military body within the HVO, that is the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certain competencies were also enjoyed by the President of the HZ H-B, not the HVO directly, but as far as I can remember, the same person held two offices, the President of the HZ H-B and the President of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's like the commander in chief of US armed forces; he is both a civil leader, the President, and he is the Commander In Chief of the armed forces. Are you familiar with that concept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In principle, yes, but I find it difficult to make such comparisons between a state which is based on a democratically established system and, on the other hand, a state which is in the process of coming into being.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right now I'm not asking you about the democratic or undemocratic foundation of HZ H-B, but I would like as succinct an answer to the question as you can give me. As of the date of any of the documents in Exhibit 38 did all authority within HZ H-B pass to the military body within the HVO, that is the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you characterise the HZ H-B at any time as of the date of any of the documents in Exhibit 38 as a military totalitarian state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could characterise the HZ H-B as an authoritarian or, if you wish, totalitarian state. As far as the other adjective is concerned, that it was a military regime, I could not fully claim that. In many aspects that were such elements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it that your answer to the question: "Would you characterise the HZ H-B as a military totalitarian state?", your answer to that question is "no"; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By definition these two adjectives, "military" and "totalitarian", do not have to go together invariably. Therefore if you are asking if it was a totalitarian regime my answer is yes. If you are asking if it was a military regime, my answer would be not fully a military regime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was a military totalitarian state? Can you answer "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, I think that you asked the question several times. You got the answer that obviously the witness wishes to give. I would suggest at this point that we could suspend the hearing and resume at 11 o'clock. (10.45 am) (Short break) (11.00 am)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Please have the accused brought in. Have the witness brought in, too, please. (Accused re-enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you have an objection, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I have no objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will note on the transcript that do you not have an objection. (Witness re-enters court).

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I have a request. My learned friend Mr. HARMON has spoken to me in the break and has stated that a matter of some urgency has arisen in the break that requires your attention and your brother judges and he has stated he would like a closed session at the end of this hearing for approximately fifteen minutes when the matter can be raised by him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Which involves the Blaskic case?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It has to be in camera?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. All right. That will be all the more reason to make sure that the questions that are asked are succinct. All right. Mr. Hayman, would you go on, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Dr. Pajic, on 2nd July you and Mr. Nobilo discussed whether there was a sufficient defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina by an army of Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time of the Serb attack, and you said, and I'm reading from a transcript of that hearing: "Some areas were defended better and some worse. I can only speak from my personal experience in Sarajevo, which defended itself from invasion. Whether that was done by the well-organised, prepared in advance army of Bosnia-Herzegovina I do not know". Do you recall generally that testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with the statement that at the time, at least in June 1992, at the time of attacks on Sarajevo, there was no army present to return the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I can recall is that there was an army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Even a commander of the general staff was appointed, Mr. Stefavic. Defence operations were carried out, but all that I'm telling you is -- belongs to memoirs, as I said yesterday, and everything else I could say by way of response is something that could be based on the knowledge acquired in my Sarajevo apartment. Movement was very difficult and I didn't have any direct knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could a document, your Honour, be marked for identification and provided to the witness? Perhaps it could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It is a document I have, your Honour. I have copies for the court and the Prosecution. Dr. Pajic, this is a copy of an article that appeared in the Manchester Guardian Weekly on June 7th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. May I take the document from here? It's easier for me to read it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. Why don't you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you turn this off for me, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could satisfy yourself that it is the news article, and then I would like to call your attention to the top of the second page of the article, which should be highlighted in yellow for you. First of all, did you write this article?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you -- strike that. Were you interviewed for this article?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So a reporter called you over the telephone and you spoke --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Could the interpreters give me as close as translation as possible of the part which is being discussed now?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Perhaps the yellow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do all of the interpretation booths have this article?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: They do, your Honour, in relevant part. Perhaps they could translate the highlighted paragraph for the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I have more or less understood, but still I would like to have this translated. The reason I asked it to be put on the ELMO is that it would be a way of having a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. So you were interviewed for this piece; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you -- did you make the statements depicted in the first paragraph of the second page? Again it's marked page 45 in the upper right-hand corner, but I believe it is the second page of this print-out of the story?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The statement that is contained in the first paragraph is basically, I think, a true reflection of what I said. Actually I have to explain that this interview was conducted under very unusual circumstances. Ms. Hela Pik, the foreign policy editor of The Guardian, phoned me and she found me in my Sarajevo apartment while the city was being shelled. There were explosions all over. I gave this interview over the telephone under very dramatic conditions. So it is very difficult for me to recall each and every word now and I have not had a look at this text for a long time now, for four or five years, so I cannot exactly confirm that all of it is absolutely accurate, but basically I think that is what is contained in this text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thinking back to the terrible events of the period of time in which you were interviewed, did you believe at that time and feel at that time that, in fact: "There is no army to return the attack"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that your question is not very precise, because you have to understand that the attack on Sarajevo was made exclusively by heavy artillery. In that sense the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina could not return the attack, because it did not have any heavy weapons of its own, so that they could from the centre of the city, the centre of Sarajevo, fire back at the heavy artillery which was deployed on the hills and mountains around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in your testimony of the 2nd that whether the Defence of Sarajevo was done by a well-organised, prepared in advance army of BiH I do not know. Does this article in the Manchester Guardian weekly refresh your recollection that the Bosnian Territorial Defence Force was only created after the war began?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that this part of my statement is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if you could take up Exhibit 38 once again shall the excerpts of the Narodni list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Before we move to the binder, this is a prosecution witness and will be given what number -- rather its exhibit number. This will be number 38. All right. This is D1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do you have Exhibit 38, Dr. Pajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The notebook?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you give me the page, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you turn to tab 2, page 5 of the English, tab 2, page 5 of the English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to return to the earlier subject of the nature of the legislative body and powers within the HVO. Directing your attention to Article 2, does this state that the HVO is a temporary body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which will cease with the establishment of regular executive authority and administration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is your interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the words "shall cease"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Article 2?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Article 2, at least in the English translation I'm reading from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I read the Croat text, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could you identify both the document and the article? I wasn't able to follow. Tell me where we are, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, your Honour. I do not have an index of the English and the French, so I'm not able to give the court page guidance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, perhaps you could help.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could direct you to the portion which my learned friend is referring to, it is, in fact, index 2 in the binder before you and it's page 5, which is the statutory decision on the temporary organisation of executive authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Excuse me, Mr. Hayman. You can continue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Article 2, Dr. Pajic. You were going to read, I think, your untranslated version so we could hear the contemporaneous translations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The HVO is a temporary body whose authority will be exercised until the moment regular executive authority and administration are established."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see under Article 7 that the types of members of the "HVO" as described in this decision are listed? This is also on the same page in the English version, Article 7?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It identifies the President, Vice-president, department head and other members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do those types of individuals -- is that characteristic of a civil body as opposed to a military body or an army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next page, Article 16, and it is the next page in the English translation do you see the first sentence of that Article states: "The HVO shall conduct its business in sessions"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that also characteristic of a civil body, not an army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know the way in which military organs operate, for example army staffs, whether they work in session, as you say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the third sentence of Article 16, which states: "The HVO shall decide by a majority vote ...". Would you agree that that is characteristic of a civil legislative type body, not an army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you told us in the first day of your testimony that you had been asked by the Prosecution to explain the division of competency and the scope of jurisdiction regarding relations between the Presidency of HZ H-B and the HVO, firstly; secondly, to explain the legal position of the armed forces of the HZ H-B, as well as the organisation of the judiciary and the executive branches. Based on your study of these documents, are you able to set forth with precision the relationship between the Presidency of the HZ H-B and both the civil and military elements within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In determining this relationship, the documents, the acts of the HZ H-B have a certain degree of imprecision. The basic one I wish to draw your attention to is that the Presidency -- if I can take you back to this decision on the establishment of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, I think that it is the same section of this document, namely it is document 2, page 3, where it says in Article 7, paragraph 2: "The President of the HZ H-B consists of the representatives of the Croatian people and the municipal bodies of authority, the senior official of the municipal body of the HVO". This shows a lack of provision. It shows that the HVO at the same time takes part in the Presidency. The other imprecision that can be seen from the later documents is that Mr. Mate Boban signs documents simultaneously as the President of the HZ H-B or, if you wish, the President of the Presidency, because it was not precisely spelt out whether the Presidency has its President or not, and at the same time he signs these documents as the President of the HVO. So, to go back to your question, it is rather difficult to make this distinction. I think that there is a lot of overlapping involved between the Presidency as the legislative authority and the HVO as executive, administrative and the supreme defence structure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given that the accused in this case was a military officer, you can appreciate that it's important that all of us gain as much insight as we can into the structure of this entity and entities that were created in Herceg-Bosna. You have an easel to your left with a black felt tip pen placed on it. Are you able to show us graphically what the relationship between the military and civilian elements of the entity described generally throughout these documents as the HVO, what the elements -- what the relationship between those elements was at any particular point of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With all due respect for the court, I always felt rather embarrassed if I had to draw anything, because throughout my academic career I either spoke or wrote, so that I really cannot make a graphic description of what you are asking me to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then if I may ask, perhaps there is a mobile unit of the headsets that I can utilise, and I will do the drawing for you, Dr. Pajic. You can instruct me how graphically you answer the question when you were asked by the Prosecution at the beginning of your study to explain the legal position of the armed forces of the HZ H-B. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness was never asked to graphically represent anything for the Prosecutor. There was never that type of request. It was simply his expert opinion that was asked for. So I object to this process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to confer for a moment with my colleagues. (Pause) the Tribunal will confer when a new issue comes up so that for the future there would be a definitive decision. The Tribunal considers that Mr. Hayman is absolutely entitled to ask for a graphical representation of his question, after which the witness will express himself. The Tribunal does not, of course, want the Tribunal to repeat his entire testimony (sic). We can then talk about the drawing, which will be tendered as an exhibit into the record. Mr. Hayman, take your pen and then remember that you have to watch the hour, and allow us to move forward. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. So, Dr. Pajic, keeping in mind that we are all very interested in the position of the military element or elements within the HVO, can you help us diagram how that military entry or body related to these other supreme and more superior powers of a civil, political, administrative, executive, of whatever nature, within the entity described in these documents and decrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, you are the one who is doing the drawer, though; correct? You are the drawer and then you will ask for comment from the witness. He was not here -- he is not here to make drawings. I simply said you have the right to illustrate your question by using graphic representation. Of course, you are the artist. You are the one who has to do the drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Absolutely, your Honour, and though I am sure my drawing is no better than Dr. Pajic's, I accept his declination to be the drawer. Do you agree we could begin with the Presidency of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, could the board be moved so that the witness can actually see what Mr. Hayman is doing?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can the public gallery see the drawing as well? That isn't possible. Put the easel in such a way that the accused and the witness can see it and the public should be able to see it as well. I do not know whether the technicians can do all of that skilful work.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: You have drawn a box representing the HVO Presidency. Do you have an opinion or can you give me any direction as to what box might appear below? In other words did the Presidency have a hierarchical relationship with, for example, the departments that were created within the HVO, the Defence Department, the Interior Department, Finance and so forth? Do you agree with the idea that we draw a straight line down from the Presidency that would then branch out and identify, for example, the different departments of the HVO or do you feel that would not be an accurate representation of your opinions and conclusions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not quite clear why you put HVO above the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shall I cross it out? Is it the HZ H-B Presidency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we would have done if you had been the draftsman, Dr. Pajic, but nonetheless continuing with my handicaps, can you give us an opinion or some direction as to what body or bodies would exist below the Presidency in a hierarchical relationship?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, I would like to go back to your last comment. I understand that you were going to make the drawing and then you would ask for comment afterwards. If the witness agrees to do the drawing, all right, but what I do not want is this questioning and answering going on for an excessively long period. Either you do the drawing with a comment from the witness. If the witness agrees to, you can also make the drawing and make the comments afterwards. What would you prefer, Mr. Pajic? Would you like to work together in order to work more quickly with defence counsel? We do not want to make you uncomfortable here. We simply want you to be comfortable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to work, collaborate with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Then do what you need so that you can get up and work together with the Defence in order to make the drawing and things will move more quickly that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Pajic. My goal is to -- whatever drawing we produce, it as accurately as possible reflects your views, opinions and judgements. Can you give me some direction? Is there an entity or body you believe would fall below the Presidency in a hierarchical relationship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My conclusion is that there is no hierarchy between the Presidency and the HVO for the simple reason that the HVO was included in the Presidency, and the same person was exercising the function of the President of HZ H-B and the President of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then perhaps we could identify in the drawing the constituent parts of the Presidency, the municipal HVO representatives and the others pursuant to tab -- Exhibit 38, tab 2, page 3, Article 7?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, therefore, those elements are whom? The representatives of the Croatian people in the municipal bodies of authority, is that one category?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how shall we term those? Municipal political leaders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Municipal Presidents of HVO bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are those the only members of the Presidency as you construe Article 7, or are there other members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not quite clear if there is a distinction between Croat people in the municipal authority and those who are exercising the function of the Presidency of the municipal HVO according to Article 7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I make a proposal? Yesterday you told Mr. Nobilo that you believed that the municipal Croatian Defence Councils were civil bodies. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that whatever HVO representatives were in the Presidency are from those municipal HVO councils or HVO elements; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we draw on the bottom of the Presidency perhaps a box that refers to civil municipal HVO representatives, something like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now we have depicted a civil HVO membership in the Presidency. Again going downstream or below this Presidency for the moment, do you have an opinion, conclusion or can you make a recommendation concerning what other bodies, such as departments, or the military element within the HVO, would that lie below the Presidency in a hierarchical relationship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may, with due respect, Mr. Hayman insists on this division between civil and military characteristics of the HVO, and I agree that the lower we go towards the municipalities, HVO seems to be exercising certain competencies on the municipal level as a civil authority, but I would like to draw your attention to the decree on armed forces of HZ H-B, page 12 in the Croat text, where it says in the first article, and I will quote from my original: "By this decree the rights and duties of citizens are regulated, the competencies of the Croatian Defence Council, of administrative bodies and legal entities in defending the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and other matters of importance to the defence system". I cited this Article, this provision, in order to draw attention to the fact that by a decree on the armed forces the rights and duties of the Croatian Defence Council are being regulated, which defence counsel insists is a civilian body. I am hereby trying to indicate that the overlapping between organs of civilian authority and the military hierarchy was so firm, they were intertwined together, that it is very difficult to make this distinction. That is why in my expert opinion I insisted on the fact that authority was centralised in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in that sense. Doing my best to co-operate with Mr. Hayman's efforts to graphically represent this situation, I appeal to you once again to re-examine my general conclusions and the quotation that I have just made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Tribunal does not want to go back to all the statements regarding this complex problem having to do with the distribution or rather with the civilian and military sides of this issue. I believe that the witness has already explained himself at great length on this subject. Questions were asked. Mr. Nobilo went back to this problem.
